raw_segments.text: Brutus, you have done that you should be sorry for.
There is no terror, Cassius, in your threats, for I am armed so strong in honesty that they
pass by me as the idle wind, which I respect not.
I did send to you for certain sums of gold, which you denied me, for I can raise no money
By heaven I had rather coin my heart and drop my blood for drachmas than to wring from the
hard hands of peasants their vile trash by any indirection.
I did send to you for gold to pay my legions, which you denied me.
Should I have answered Caius Cassius so?
When Marcus Brutus grows so covetous, to lock such rascal counters from his friends, be
ready, gods, with all your thunderbolts, dash him to pieces.
